title: A finite intermediate algebra capturing finite separable residue subfields
statement: Let $A\to D$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $D$ is integral over $A$, meaning that every element satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be prime, put $k=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$, and suppose the primes of $D$ above $\mathfrak p$ form a finite set $\{\mathfrak r_1,\ldots,\mathfrak r_t\}$ without repetitions (possibly $t=0$). Put $E_i=\operatorname{Frac}(D/\mathfrak r_i)$ with its induced $k$-embedding. For every $i$, suppose a subfield $F_i\subseteq E_i$ containing $k$ is given such that $F_i/k$ is finite-dimensional and separable (minimal polynomials have no repeated roots), and $E_i/F_i$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. There exists a subring $C\subseteq D$ containing the image of $A$, finite as an $A$-module, such that contraction induces a bijection from the primes of $D$ above $\mathfrak p$ to the primes of $C$ above $\mathfrak p$. Writing $\mathfrak s_i=C\cap\mathfrak r_i$, the field $\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak s_i)$, viewed inside $E_i$ by inclusion, contains $F_i$, is finite-dimensional over $k$, and $E_i/\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak s_i)$ is purely inseparable. Moreover $D$ is integral over $C$.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, lemma-etale-makes-integral-split, first proof, finite intermediate algebra S-prime capturing the separable residue subfields and distinguishing the fibre primes. A fraction-numerator/denominator variant avoids the preliminary localization and Chinese remainder theorem.

proof.text: For each pair $i<j$, the distinct primes $\mathfrak r_i,\mathfrak r_j$ have the same contraction $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability], neither contains the other. Choose $z_{ij}\in\mathfrak r_i\setminus\mathfrak r_j$. There are only finitely many such elements. They will distinguish the contractions once they are included in $C$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00GT, lemma-integral-no-inclusion; explicit pairwise separating elements in the finite-model construction of Tag 0BSR.

proof.text: For each $i$, choose a finite $k$-spanning family $f_{i1},\ldots,f_{in_i}$ of $F_i$, using the meaning of finite-dimensional in [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Every $f_{ia}\in E_i=\operatorname{Frac}(D/\mathfrak r_i)$ can be written $\overline u_{ia}/\overline v_{ia}$ with $u_{ia},v_{ia}\in D$ and $v_{ia}\notin\mathfrak r_i$: choose numerator and nonzero denominator in $D/\mathfrak r_i$ and lift each to $D$. Take all these numerators and denominators, for every $i,a$, together with all $z_{ij}$ from step 1. This is a finite set $T\subseteq D$. No simultaneous residue lifting or Chinese remainder theorem is needed.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, lemma-etale-makes-integral-split, first proof, choice of residue-field generators; fraction representatives and a finite spanning family replace its primitive-element and localization choices.

proof.text: Let $C$ be the $A$-subalgebra of $D$ generated by $T$, namely the subring consisting of polynomial expressions in elements of $T$ with coefficients in the image of $A$. Thus $C\subseteq D$ contains that image. Every element of $T$ is integral over $A$ by the hypothesis on $D$. Apply [lem-sc-finite-generated-integral-subring] to this finite set to conclude that $C$ is finite as an $A$-module. If $t=0$, take $T=\varnothing$; then $C$ is just the image of $A$, still finite as an $A$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00GM, lemma-characterize-integral, forward implication and its bounded-monomial proof; Tag 02JJ, lemma-characterize-finite-in-terms-of-integral; used for S-prime in Tag 0BSR.

proof.text: For any $d\in D$, take a monic relation $d^n+a_{n-1}d^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0=0$ with coefficients in the image of $A$. Since those coefficients lie in $C$, exactly the same relation proves $d$ integral over $C$. Hence $D$ is integral over $C$. Contraction of $\mathfrak r_i$ gives a prime $\mathfrak s_i=\mathfrak r_i\cap C$ over $\mathfrak p$: inverse images of proper prime ideals are prime, since a product maps into the ideal only if one factor does. For $i<j$, $z_{ij}\in C$ belongs to $\mathfrak s_i$ but not $\mathfrak s_j$, so these contractions are pairwise distinct.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, lemma-etale-makes-integral-split, first proof, integrality over S-prime and distinct contractions; monic equations and separating witnesses written out.

proof.text: The inclusion $C\hookrightarrow D$ is injective, and step 4 proves it integral. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] applies. Given any prime $\mathfrak s$ of $C$ over $\mathfrak p$, choose a prime $\mathfrak r$ of $D$ contracting to $\mathfrak s$. Its contraction to $A$ is $\mathfrak p$, by composing inverse images, so $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak r_i$ for some $i$ by the complete list in the hypothesis. Hence $\mathfrak s=\mathfrak s_i$. Together with the pairwise distinction, this proves the required bijection. It also handles $t=0$: a prime of $C$ over $\mathfrak p$ would lift to a forbidden prime of $D$.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, lemma-etale-makes-integral-split, first proof, surjectivity of Spec(S) to Spec(S-prime), citing Algebra Tag 00GQ, lemma-integral-overring-surjective.

proof.text: Fix i and put s_i = r_i ∩ C. The inclusion induces the canonical map of residue fields Ideal.ResidueField.map. Its composite with the residue-field map from A agrees with the given k-embedding, checked on A by Ideal.ResidueField.ringHom_ext and map_algebraMap. Since C is module-finite over A, the Mathlib instance Algebra.QuasiFinite.instFiniteResidueField gives that kappa(s_i) is finite-dimensional over k. The private helper residue_finite identifies its scalar module with the explicit map.toAlgebra.toModule by Module.ext' and quotient representatives. Form the algebra homomorphism f : kappa(s_i) →ₐ[k] E_i and take its fieldRange as L_i. AlgHom.equivFieldRange transports finite-dimensionality to L_i; its underlying subfield is definitionally the required fieldRange. This is the existing finite-residue-field API for the span argument in the original plan.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, lemma-etale-makes-integral-split, first proof, finite-model residue fields; Algebra Tag 00GS, lemma-integral-over-field, first assertion, and the explicit span of module generators.

proof.text: For every $a$, both $u_{ia}$ and $v_{ia}$ lie in $C$, and the latter has nonzero image in $C/\mathfrak s_i$ because $v_{ia}\notin\mathfrak r_i$. Thus $f_{ia}=\overline u_{ia}/\overline v_{ia}\in L_i$. Since these elements span $F_i$ over $k$ and $k\subseteq L_i$, this proves $F_i\subseteq L_i\subseteq E_i$. In characteristic $p>0$, every $x\in E_i$ has $x^{p^n}\in F_i$ for some $n$ by the assumed pure inseparability and [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]; the same power lies in $L_i$, so $E_i/L_i$ is purely inseparable. In characteristic zero the assumption says $E_i=F_i$, forcing $L_i=E_i$. This gives all remaining assertions; if $t=0$, these residue-field assertions have no indices and are vacuous.
